identificationModule.briefTitle: Dydrogesterone Versus GnRH Antagonist in Poor Responders Undergoing Double Ovarian Stimulation
identificationModule.officialTitle: Dydrogesterone Versus GnRH Antagonist in Poor Responders Undergoing Double Ovarian Stimulation: A Randomized Controlled Non-inferiority Trial

descriptionModule.briefSummary: The aim of this randomized controlled trial is to compare the efficacy and cost-effectiveness of using progestin with GnRH antagonist to prevent premature LH surge in poor responders undergoing double stimulation protocol.

armGroups.label: Progestin primed ovarian stimulation group
armGroups.description:
HMG ( 300IU) was used during the follicular phase of ovarian stimulation (FPS) and during the luteal phase of ovarian stimulation (LPS). Progestin (dydrogesterone) 30 mg/day was used to prevent premature LH surge during the FPS and LPS.

In subsequent cycle, frozen embryo transfer was done

armGroups.label: GnRH antagonist group
armGroups.description:
HMG ( 300IU) was used during the follicular phase of ovarian stimulation (FPS) and during the luteal phase of ovarian stimulation (LPS). Flexible GnRH antagonist protocol (Cetrorelix acetate) (0.2 mg) was used to prevent premature LH surge during the FPS and LPS.

In subsequent cycle, frozen embryo transfer was done

primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Ten to fifteen days after starting ovarian stimulation]

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Patients belonging to Poseidon group 4

Exclusion Criteria:

* PCOS
* Endometriosis
* History of recurrent abortion
